prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and the cereblon-dependent mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues.

statement.case_for: I have moved my preferred configuration from halide perovskites (B005) to targeted protein degradation (B020). The first round showed that the objections I raised against B005 myself (unresolved stability, lead toxicity, manufacturing, and credit that cannot be fitted into three names without omitting Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis) were shared by Aili, Aqvist, Chabes, Linke, Sparr and Zou, and none of them answered those objections. B020 is the only candidate in which five members independently place the same achievement in their preferred prize, and the scientific case is strong: a designed molecule induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a target, so that the target is ubiquitylated and destroyed catalytically. This event-driven mode of action is a new chemical principle, it reaches proteins that occupancy-based inhibitors cannot, and it has been reproduced in many laboratories. The coherent credit is Crews and Deshaies for the founding concept and early demonstrations, and Handa for identifying cereblon as the target of thalidomide, which explains why thalidomide-type drugs act as molecular glues and supplies the E3 ligase handle used in most clinical-stage degraders. This is the one strand of the field already attached to approved drugs, so it directly answers the maturity objection that colleagues have raised against B020.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC has been approved, so clinical payoff for the heterobifunctional strand remains prospective, and a prize could look early if trials disappoint. Attribution is the hard part: with three names Ciulli (structure-guided VHL ligand and ternary-complex design), Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray are excluded, and Ciulli's absence weakens the molecular-design strand, as Aili and Aqvist argue. Combining PROTACs and glues in one citation also risks being read as two discoveries under one heading. Finally, my own field of study is far from this area, so I judge it on the committee record and not on personal expertise.

responses.point: Linke prefers Ciulli to Handa because a PROTAC-centred citation describes one coherent invention, while a Handa slot shifts the prize toward glues where credit spreads across Ito, Handa, Gray and others.
responses.response: The argument is fair, and I accept that the glue strand has no clean three-person split of its own. But the cereblon mechanism is not a separate line next to PROTACs. Cereblon is the E3 ligase handle for most degraders now in the clinic, and thalidomide-type drugs are the only members of the field in patients today. So the citation does not need to cover all glue chemistry. It only needs to credit the discovery that made cereblon-based degradation understandable and usable. Your own point that this strand is the only one attached to approved drugs is, for me, the reason it should be in the citation. If a majority prefers a PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli, I could accept that, and I would rather see the committee settle on one definition than a split vote on the third name.

responses.point: Aili says Handa's work is a target-identification result about an existing drug and not a design principle that chemists could generalise, whereas Ciulli's VHL work made heterobifunctional degraders designable.
responses.response: I agree that Ciulli's work is the stronger contribution to design chemistry, and that a Handa choice leaves that strand unrecognised. I still do not accept that identification of cereblon is only a target-identification result. It explained how a small molecule can redirect an E3 ligase toward new substrates, which is the mechanistic basis that glue-degrader design later built on, and it created the ligand class that many PROTACs use. You said you could support Handa if the committee wants glues in the citation. My position is that it should, because otherwise the prize is defined by chemistry that has no approved drug yet. We differ on weighting, not on facts, and I do not claim that the Handa choice is free of cost.

responses.point: Aqvist would pick Ciulli over Handa for a PROTAC-centred prize and accept that the glue story waits another year, while noting that the lack of an approved degrader could make the prize look rushed.
responses.response: The risk of a rushed prize is the most serious point against B020 and I do not dismiss it. My view is that it is smaller if the citation includes the cereblon strand, since approved drugs then stand behind the award, and larger for a PROTAC-only prize where the clinical test is still pending. Deferring the glue story by a year also has a cost, because it would then need a separate prize with the same Crews and Deshaies mechanism behind it. I also note that your concern about perovskites matches mine, and I have given up B005 as my preferred candidate for the reasons you and others stated.

responses.point: Sparr pairs B049 (Cullis for ionizable lipid nanoparticles) with Crews and Deshaies for the PROTAC concept, arguing that the two achievements are distinct and that the 2023 Medicine prize recognised the nucleoside modifications and not the carrier.
responses.response: The chemistry in lipid nanoparticles (pKa-tuned ionizable lipids, phase behaviour, endosomal escape) is real and I do not regard it as only pharmaceutical technology. My difficulty is attribution, which you acknowledge yourself: Cullis alone understates the work of Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and industrial optimisation was decisive. Adding B049 would also leave B020 with two names and exclude Handa entirely, which I think weakens the part where the committee agrees most. I prefer one well-supported part with three names to two parts where each is under-credited.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can agree on a single third name for B020 (Handa or Ciulli) and whether the citation covers cereblon glues or PROTACs only.
Whether the absence of an approved heterobifunctional degrader is a decisive timing objection for a prize now.
Whether the support for B020 reflects convergence on the topic more than on the prize as it would be worded, given that five supporters propose three different sets of names.
Whether perovskite solar cells (B005) will mature in stability and credit clarity to become the stronger candidate in a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, but no shortlisted candidate has a documented connection to me; my own research area, biological energy conversion, is not a shortlisted topic and I have no tie to any credited name.
